title: Manuscript production: a readiness checklist with no winner
objective: Report whether a chapter or volume is ready for production: references resolve and match their citations, cross-references and numbering hold, the style sheet is followed, every figure and table is called out, and the permissions list is complete. This is a checklist gauntlet. It names no winner and ranks nothing.
audience: Set per bout: the managing editor who releases the manuscript to production, and the author who fixes what is found.

candidate_inputs.candidate: one manuscript version: a Markdown or plain-text file for the chapter or volume, plus its bibliography file or files (flat file names)
candidate_inputs.style_sheet: The house rules, written as machine-readable style rules where possible (spelling, capitalisation, hyphenation, number style, heading levels, reference form).
candidate_inputs.figure_table_inventory: Every figure and table, with its file, caption and source.
candidate_inputs.permissions_ledger: Every third-party figure, table, long quotation and epigraph, with the rights holder, the status (cleared, pending, not needed) and the date.

officials.why: A citation with no entry, or an entry nobody cites, is a production defect. Checked on bytes, offline.
Whether each reference exists in public registries. Published detectors have real false-positive rates, so single-source absence is a prompt for a person, never a blocker.
Cross-references such as 'see Chapter 4' or 'Figure 2.3' must resolve, and chapter, section, figure, table and note numbering must run in sequence.
Violations of rules the house wrote down and marked as errors. Warnings are advisory. The rules are the editor's; the check enforces them and says nothing of quality.
Every figure and table must be called out in the text and every callout must point to one that exists, with a caption and a file.
Every third-party item in the inventory needs a ledger row with a status of cleared or not needed. A missing or pending row blocks release.
Link rot in references and notes. Reported for the editor; an unreachable site may be down today.
Spelling and grammar rule hits beyond the style sheet, as leads for the copyeditor.

evidence_required: The style sheet, figure and table inventory and permissions ledger, hashed.
The manuscript version's exact bytes, hashed. A re-edited manuscript is a new version.
For every blocking item: the official, its version, the location in the manuscript and the rule or ledger row concerned.
For every item the check could not complete: the reason, reported as unverified.
hard_disqualifiers: A citation has no reference entry, or a reference entry that matches it badly.
A cross-reference or a numbering sequence is broken.
A style-sheet rule marked as an error is violated.
A figure or table has no callout, or a callout has no figure or table.
A third-party item has no cleared permissions row.

judge_qualifications.model_judges: none. No model judges the manuscript; the event has no panel and no bracket.
judge_qualifications.reviewers: A copyeditor or production editor works through the blocking items and the leads. The style sheet is only as good as the rules the house has written down.

format.why: Production readiness is a set of pass or fail facts about one manuscript, not a preference between manuscripts. Several versions may be checked, but each receives its own report and none is ranked. The unit of output is a list of blockers and leads.
format.report: One outcome per official per manuscript version: pass, fail, unverified or not applicable, with locations.

no_clear_winner_when: this event never names a winner; every run ends in a readiness report
a check could not run (INCONCLUSIVE for that item, listed as unverified and never as a pass)
an input needed by a decisive official is missing, such as the permissions ledger (INCONCLUSIVE; the manuscript is not reported ready)

human_evidence_boundary: Whether the manuscript is correct, well argued or fit to publish. Readiness is not editorial acceptance.
Whether a reference supports the claim it is cited for. A reference can exist and match its citation and still not say what the text says it does.
Whether permissions are legally sufficient. The ledger shows a row and a status; rights holders and counsel decide whether the grant covers the use.
Whether the style sheet is complete. Unwritten house habits are not checked.
Whether the figures and tables are accurate and legible in print or on screen.

privacy.notes: The officials run locally. Unpublished manuscripts are usually internal or restricted. The reference-resolution and link officials contact public registries and sites, so they stay off until the owner clears the outgoing queries.

notes: SPECIFIED, NOT RUNNABLE. To make it runnable build: ms.citations_match_refs on pybtex (MIT) or bibtexparser (MIT), with citeproc-py (BSD-2-Clause-Views per PyPI) or pandoc for citation parsing, and AnyStyle (licence text BSD-2-style, SPDX not confirmed) or GROBID (Apache-2.0) if references arrive as free text; avoid citeproc-js (CPAL-1.0 OR AGPL-3.0). ms.references_resolve on bibtex-updater (MIT; contacts Crossref, OpenAlex and arXiv). ms.xref_numbering on markdownlint (MIT) plus custom resolvers. ms.style_sheet on Vale (MIT, offline), with the house rules written as Vale styles; no study was found showing that Vale scores track quality, so it enforces rules and no more. ms.figure_table_callouts and ms.permissions_complete are custom with no upstream. ms.links on lychee (Apache-2.0 OR MIT). ms.language_leads on LanguageTool run as a local server (LGPL-2.1; avoid its GPL-3.0 Python wrapper). Schema gaps: the controller vocabulary has no status for a checklist that finishes without a winner, and 'disqualify' here means 'blocks release'.
